CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidney stones

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male who presents with a one-week history of kidney stone. One week ago, while working in a barn moving hay, he developed sudden onset severe pain in his right back that radiated almost to his groin. Associated symptoms included diaphoresis and nausea. He was evaluated by his PCP who ordered a CT scan confirming the presence of a kidney stone. This is his first episode of kidney stones. Since the initial presentation, he has experienced intermittent pain of lesser duration and severity. He has been straining his urine without visualizing any stone fragments. He denies hematuria or dark-colored urine.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies fever, chills, or other systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No prior kidney stones

MEDICATIONS
Not documented

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Father with history of recurrent kidney stones

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works with horses in a barn setting, involving manual labor with hay

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Afebrile, normal blood pressure and heart rate
Abdomen: Soft, no tenderness to palpation, no rebound or guarding. Right costovertebral angle tenderness present.

RESULTS
CT scan: 0.5 cm stone located in the proximal right ureter. No hydronephrosis.
Lab tests ordered: BMP, urinalysis, and urine culture

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Kidney stone, 0.5 cm in proximal right ureter without obstruction or hydronephrosis. Plan: (1) Increase fluid intake to facilitate urination and stone passage; (2) Oxycodone 5 mg every 6-8 hours for pain management; (3) Acetaminophen for breakthrough pain between oxycodone doses; (4) Continue straining urine; (5) Pending urinalysis and urine culture; consider antibiotics if infection identified; (6) Follow-up in 1-2 weeks; (7) If stone has not passed at follow-up, consider lithotripsy as treatment option.
